A0001.explanation: If you have lived in your rental for at least 12 months, your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you and must state it in writing. Local rule Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC) Sections 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5 governs; state rule yields. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2, retrieved 2026-10-01.

In Los Angeles, landlords can only evict tenants for specific legal reasons like not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord or family needs to move in. all coverage conditions met. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC) Sections 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5, retrieved 2026-10-01.

If your landlord wants to evict you to demolish your unit for new construction, they must notify the city, give you written notice, and pay you relocation assistance that is higher for lower income tenants. coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to Protected Units that are residential dwelling units subject to rent or price control or rented by lower income households within the past five years, or withdrawn under Ellis Act within past 10 years. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Sections 151.22-151.28, 165.03.I(1); Ordinances #188481 and #188482, retrieved 2026-10-01.

In California, landlords cannot discriminate based on your income source or credit history unfairly. If you have a government rent subsidy, they must consider your ability to pay using alternative proof, not just credit scores. all coverage conditions met. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955, retrieved 2026-10-01.

Your landlord can only ask for a security deposit up to one month's rent unless special conditions apply. They must keep it safe, only use it for allowed reasons like unpaid rent or damages beyond normal wear, and return any leftover money within 21 days after you move out with an itemized list of deductions. Local rule Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance governs; state rule yields. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5, retrieved 2026-10-01. Unknown because the data lacks: owner_type.

If you are evicted for a no-fault reason, your landlord must pay you relocation assistance based on your income, age, length of tenancy, and property type. coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants displaced by no-fault evictions under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance in Los Angeles. Source: LAMC 151.09, 165.06, retrieved 2026-10-01.

If your landlord evicts you for demolition, they must pay you relocation assistance within 15 days of notice, with higher amounts for lower income tenants. coverage conditions could not be machine-checked: Applies to tenants of units covered by RSO, JCO, or State Housing Crisis Act, especially lower income tenants under the Resident Protections Ordinance. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Sections 151.22-151.28; Ordinances #188481 and #188482; California Government Code Section 66300 et seq., retrieved 2026-10-01.

If you rent a unit covered by the Los Angeles RSO, your landlord must pay you interest on your security deposit. all coverage conditions met. Source: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, retrieved 2026-10-01.
